transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Devon Li (Redwood SE), Markus Hale (CTO, ZenPath), Priya Sen (ML Engineer, ZenPath), Liam O'Neill (Product)

Summary:
Short demo of Redwood Hosted API focused on chat/text generation basics - streaming responses, request params (temperature, max_tokens), retry behavior and idempotency, and basic cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer asked about security (SOC2, encryption), VPC/on-prem options, and running a small latency benchmark.

Topics:
- Hosted API overview and model catalog
- Streaming and partial response consumption
- Key generation params and recommended defaults
- Retries, idempotency keys, and best practices for at-least-once vs at-most-once behavior
- Observability in Console (token breakdown, latency by route)
- Next steps: pricing, security docs, POC scoping

Transcript:
00:00 Ava Martinez: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're on for about 45 to 60 minutes today, gonna show Hosted API chat and text generation basics and then leave time for Qs. Devon's gonna do the deep parts.
00:08 Markus Hale: Great, thanks Ava. Quick background - we're building a prompt-engineing layer for analytics reports, want low latency for interactive product and cheaper batch exports for nightly runs.
00:18 Ava Martinez: Perfect, yeah that's a common pattern. We'll cover streaming for interactive UI and batching/cost knobs for exports.
01:02 Devon Li: Alright opening the demo, this is the Redwood hosted API. Quick note on models - we provide a model catalog with verified perf profiles, you can pick lower-cost quantized variants or higher quality ones.
01:24 Priya Sen: When you say quantized variant, do you mean like int8 on your side, or are we responsible for anything?
01:30 Devon Li: On our side - we host quantized model builds and surface them as separate model ids. For Private/Dedicated customers there's an option to bring your own quant build but for hosted it's managed.
02:10 Devon Li: Now streaming - we'll make a chat call and show chunked responses. In code this is a server-sent event stream, you can start rendering tokens as they arrive which cuts perceived latency a lot.
02:42 Liam O'Neill: Does streaming increase cost or change billing?
02:48 Devon Li: No, billing is token-based regardless of streaming. Streaming just changes delivery semantics. One caveat: if you display partial tokens you should handle edits - sometimes early tokens get revised.
03:15 Markus Hale: How do you handle retries if a stream drops mid-response?
03:21 Devon Li: Good question - recommended pattern is to use idempotency_key on the request and a conversation_id. For streaming, if the connection drops we retry the request with same idempotency_key and Redwood will try to resume or return a completed response if available. There are limits to resumability; for exact at-most-once you should do server-side dedupe on your app layer.
04:05 Priya Sen: So is there a guarantee that we won't get duplicates for the same idempotency key?
04:10 Devon Li: We aim for at-most-once for non-streaming calls with idempotency_key, for streaming it's best-effort resume. If you need strict semantics we recommend acknowledging completed outputs in your app or use dedicated capacity where you can control queues.
04:50 Ava Martinez: For retries we also recommend exponential backoff with jitter, we expose Retry-After headers on 429/503.
05:10 Markus Hale: What's a typical retry policy you recommend?
05:14 Devon Li: Start small - 3 attempts with base backoff 200-500ms doubled each time, max backoff ~5s for interactive. For long-running batch jobs you'll want a longer backoff window.
06:00 Devon Li: Switching to request params - temperature, max_tokens, top_p, presence_penalty. Defaults we surface are conservative: temperature 0.2 for extraction/qa, 0.7 for creative. Max_tokens we recommend based on your prompt distribution.
06:35 Priya Sen: Any guidance for tokenization? We have prompts with a lot of embedded JSON and tables.
06:40 Devon Li: Try to pre-tokenize a sample set and look at distribution. Our Console shows token distribution per route which helps set max_tokens and estimate cost. Also prefix caching helps if you have common prompt templates - cache benefits are automatic for Hosted API.
07:10 Liam O'Neill: Can you explain prefix/KV cache briefly?
07:16 Devon Li: Sure - prefix caching stores the KV cache for common prefixes like system prompt + few-shot examples. For interactive chat that share the same system prompt we can reuse cached keys and shave off compute and latency.
07:40 Markus Hale: Is prefix cache available on hosted tiers?
07:45 Devon Li: Yes, automatic for most models. Dedicated gives more control over cache TTLs and eviction policies.
08:05 Priya Sen: On observability - can we see per-token cost in Console?
08:09 Ava Martinez: Yep token-level cost and latency breakdown, plus traces per request. You can also set alerts for quality regressions tied to evals and prompt sets.
08:25 Markus Hale: Security questions - are you SOC 2 and do you support KMS for encrypting keys?
08:30 Ava Martinez: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO documentation, we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit and you can bring a KMS for Dedicated/private setups. We'll share the security pack after the call.
09:05 Priya Sen: Data retention? We need logs off by default for certain customers.
09:10 Ava Martinez: You can configure retention and opt out of training on hosted for enterprise contracts; audit logs are available and configurable.
09:40 Devon Li: Back to the demo - here's a code sample for streaming in Node. (reads code) The client opens an SSE stream, we push events with token chunks and a final event when complete.
10:12 Markus Hale: If we do partial render, any risk of hallucinations mid-stream that get corrected later?
10:18 Devon Li: Yes that's possible. We recommend holding off committing to UI actions until final chunk, or show a progress indicator and allow edits.
11:05 Priya Sen: For cost estimation - can we get per-route breakdown programmatically?
11:10 Ava Martinez: Yes via the billing API and Console export. We can filter by model, route, and time window.
11:30 Liam O'Neill: One of our concerns is throughput - peak qps might be 120 qps, avg 20, with mixed short interactive requests and larger batch jobs.
11:42 Devon Li: For that pattern we usually recommend Hosted + burst to Dedicated if you hit sustained peak. Smart routing can send critical low-latency traffic to faster model variants and low-priority batch to cheaper instances.
12:10 Markus Hale: Any specific SLOs for hosted?
12:14 Ava Martinez: We publish performance profiles per model; hosted SLOs vary by region and plan. For enterprise we can talk SLAs on Dedicated.
12:40 Devon Li: Quick note on retries + idempotency - include an idempotency_key and conversation_id, also include a client_request_id if you want more traceability in logs.
13:05 Priya Sen: How do we do deterministic reruns for evaluation?
13:10 Devon Li: Use fixed seeds and temperature 0 or same top_p, and pin the model version. We support model pinning so your dev/test environments can be stable.
13:45 Ava Martinez: I'm going to show the Console quick - route dashboard, token breakdown, alerting.
14:10 Devon Li: Here is an example of a canary rollout - you can route 10% of traffic to new model or quantized variant, and auto-fallback to previous version if latency or error rate breaches threshold.
14:45 Markus Hale: Good, that helps for gradual rollouts.
15:20 Priya Sen: When you mention quantized model variants, are performance numbers in the catalog measured on typical seq len like 512?
15:27 Devon Li: Usually measured on a couple of distributions - 128, 512, 1024 - the model card includes sequence length assumptions, we can also run custom benchmarks with your payloads.
16:00 Liam O'Neill: On SDKs - we have backend Python and some client JS. Anything special to note?
16:06 Devon Li: Python and JS SDKs are fully supported; streaming examples in both. We also have rate limit headers and client utilities for backoff.
16:40 Markus Hale: Do you provide a retry middleware?
16:44 Devon Li: There's a small client-side helper in the SDK for recommended retry/backoff; we usually put business retry logic in the app.
17:10 Priya Sen: Latency numbers - can you share ballparks for 8k model on hosted?
17:16 Devon Li: Ballpark, short-seq 50-150ms token latency depending on region and model. End-to-end for short chat response 200-500ms typical on optimized models; larger sequences higher. We'll run a bench with your tokens to be precise.
17:55 Markus Hale: Good. Any hard limits for request size?
17:58 Devon Li: We have a max token limit per model (listed in model card). For very large documents we recommend chunking or embeddings + retrieval flow.
18:30 Ava Martinez: Ok quick demo of a streaming failure: I'll intentionally drop connection and show retry behavior.
18:45 Devon Li: (simulates) connection dropped, client retries with same idempotency key, server responds with completed payload since it finished behind the scenes.
19:20 Priya Sen: What if server crashed mid-inference - is there a partial result?
19:25 Devon Li: If the server crashed before completion you might get a 5xx and need to retry; using idempotency you may get the same response if the run completed, otherwise will re-run. For strict at-most-once we recommend storing results in a dedupe datastore keyed by idempotency_key.
20:10 Liam O'Neill: Any quotas per account by default?
20:14 Ava Martinez: Default rate limits apply; enterprise accounts can request higher quotas or reserved Dedicated capacity.
20:40 Markus Hale: For our POC we'd like to run 10k sample requests and see latency distribution.
20:45 Devon Li: We can run a benchmark if you provide sample prompts and token distribution; we'll share results and a spreadsheet.
21:10 Priya Sen: We'll provide sample prompts and traffic profile after this call.
21:20 Ava Martinez: Great - action items noted.

(--- mid-call, deeper technical Qs and minor crosstalk, timestamps skipped to keep capture concise)

32:05 Devon Li: Quick note on model updates - we support model version pinning and rollback. If you pin a version we keep it stable for your routes.
33:10 Markus Hale: Any costs for streaming because of open connection time?
33:14 Devon Li: No extra cost outside tokens and connection overhead is negligible. Idle connection quotas exist for some SDKs.
34:00 Priya Sen: Regarding observability - can we export traces to our DataDog?
34:05 Ava Martinez: Yes we have integrations (Datadog, NewRelic) and you can stream logs to your SIEM for audit.
35:10 Liam O'Neill: Does Redwood support SAML SSO for Console access?
35:14 Ava Martinez: Yes SSO, RBAC and SCIM provisioning are supported on enterprise plans.
36:00 Devon Li: One more note on batching - for throughput you can batch multiple prompts into a single request, Redwood's runtime optimizes for batching when possible to improve GPU utilization. But batching increases tail latency so it's a tradeoff.
36:45 Markus Hale: That fits our batch export needs.
37:20 Priya Sen: For billing, can we get a forecast for the next quarter based on token estimates?
37:25 Ava Martinez: We'll take your qps and token distribution and run a forecast - I'll include that in the pricing sheet.
38:05 Devon Li: Also we provide guidance on quantization and model choices to hit cost targets in Redwood Optimize.
38:30 Markus Hale: Competitors - we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI; interested in price/perf delta.
38:36 Ava Martinez: We can share benchmark comparisons we've run; note workloads vary a lot so we'll run one with your samples.
39:10 Priya Sen: Any legal constraints on PII in prompts?
39:15 Ava Martinez: We have policies and can configure retention/PII redaction for enterprise. We'll include legal contact in docs.
40:00 Devon Li: Wrapping up - recap of recommended defaults: streaming for interactive UI, idempotency_key + conversation_id for retries, 3 attempt backoff with jitter, use prefix caching to reduce cost for repeated prompts, pin models for determinism.
40:40 Markus Hale: That works. Next steps?
40:45 Ava Martinez: We'll send pricing/security pack, Devon will run benchmark once Priya provides prompt set, schedule POC scoping on 2026-03-28.
41:05 Liam O'Neill: Sounds good.

End of meeting recap:
- Key asks: 10k request latency benchmark, pricing for hosted + estimated Dedicated commit, security docs (SOC2/ISO, KMS options), POC scope.
- Risks called out: streaming resume not guaranteed for strict at-most-once semantics; need to design dedupe layer for critical ops.

Final note from attendee:
41:40 Priya Sen: Thanks everyone, will send prompt sets and sample traffic by EOD tomorrow.
41:50 Ava Martinez: Thanks all - talk soon.
